scope: Targeted literature and conceptual collision audit for the slow signed-service phase mechanism; no simulations, controller implementation, performance search, software download or source-code execution.
novelty_verdict: Reject the weak off-peak-phase/asymmetric-headroom novelty claim. A nontrivial GFL-BESS-specific analytical impossibility-and-recovery theorem remains unestablished; this audit does not certify a literature gap.

Zecchino and Gerini variable P/Q capability and predictive battery states
Periodic storage MPC, periodic admissibility, robust periodic tubes and power-electronic limit-cycle MPC
GFL DC-link energy, PLL interactions, limiter priorities and fault recovery through 2026-10-02
search_limits: Targeted primary-source pass, not exhaustive proof of nonexistence.
A search for cyclostationary safety did not identify a closer primary storage source; no absence claim follows from that keyword.
MDPI and Elsevier direct opens were unavailable. Publisher-indexed body passages were inspected; no new source binaries or supplements were saved.
Prior archive metadata were treated as historical and were not silently upgraded to fresh full-artifact verification.
Service phase is distinguished from PLL angle, AC fault-inception angle and twice-line-frequency power ripple.

sources.title: Service-Constrained Critical Energy-Headroom Boundaries for Current-Limited Grid-Forming Battery Converters
sources.inspection: Fresh publisher-indexed body sections and tables; direct HTML/PDF open returned 429/unavailable. Supplement not re-downloaded.
sources.defined_boundary: A trajectory classifier, positive-part service deficits, first-feasible initial event reserve, and a robust threshold requiring feasibility at every larger tested reserve; return is to constant dispatch with limiter inactivity.
sources.scope_limit: Inspected service definitions do not impose a bidirectional periodic contract or phase-indexed return to continuing forcing. Reserve is an event allocation, separate from DC capacitor energy and installed battery capacity.

sources.title: Impedance-passivity coordination of hydrogen-coupled AI data centers for oscillation damping and fault ride-through at transmission interfaces
sources.date: Issue 2027-01; first online date unresolved in this fresh pass
sources.inspection: Fresh publisher-indexed full-text passages; direct publisher open returned 403.
sources.defined_boundary: Four-variable coordination under current, APD and SOEC operating/ramp limits. DC buffer absorbs fast power while source commands are slower. Combined sustained forcing and sag recover to a forced residual.
sources.scope_limit: The inspected definitions do not provide a signed utility-BESS two-sided DC-energy/SoC impossibility sector by service phase. No fresh code or supplement inspection; no claim about absent features outside inspected text.

sources.title: Optimal Provision of Concurrent Primary Frequency and Local Voltage Control from a BESS Considering Variable Capability Curves: Modelling and Experimental Assessment
sources.defined_boundary: P/Q capability depends on AC/DC voltage and SoC; TTC internal states carry current history, with predicted DC voltage, charge/discharge conversion branches, and SoC bounds.
sources.scope_limit: One-step operating-point allocation using a 1 s discretization, not a subcycle sag/recovery certificate. Dynamic capability and internal battery memory are prior art.

sources.title: Optimal Grid-Forming Control of Battery Energy Storage Systems Providing Multiple Services: Modelling and Experimental Validation
sources.defined_boundary: Dispatch MPC predicts DC current/rate, DC voltage and SoC from current states. The real-time stage makes P/Q commands AC/DC-capability-feasible.
sources.scope_limit: 10 s MPC and 1 s reference conversion do not establish fast fault-current safety or return to a mandated continuing oscillatory service.

sources.title: Periodic constraint-tightening MPC for switched PV battery operation
sources.inspection: Fresh primary publisher full text; equation-level review also completed by the targeted periodic-safety reviewer.
sources.defined_boundary: R^i(n) constrains all future times and admissible prediction errors. F^s(n) is the periodic set of feasible initial charges. Terminal targets and readiness for a future switch are indexed by phase.
sources.scope_limit: Scalar hourly energy balance; only one primary-to-secondary schedule switch. It does not include GFL current dynamics or a separate converter DC-link energy state.

sources.title: Reference Governors and Maximal Output Admissible Sets for Linear Periodic Systems
sources.inspection: Fresh primary author full HTML; equation anchors refer to v1.
sources.defined_boundary: Omega_k depends on initial state and initial timeslot, constrains every future output and obeys cyclic predecessor relations. The governor preserves membership while modifying the requested command.
sources.scope_limit: General linear-periodic system. Holding a governed command is allowed; this is not a guarantee for an immutable signed service through a grid sag.

sources.title: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control with Limit Cycle Stability Guarantees
sources.inspection: Fresh primary author full HTML. Journal version not used for equation numbering.
sources.defined_boundary: Phase-dependent terminal sets/costs and cyclic invariant tubes establish recursive feasibility and asymptotic tracking of a selected limit cycle from feasible initial states, including power-electronics examples.
sources.scope_limit: Switched affine model with constant exogenous source. It does not jointly establish the stated GFL sag, immutable signed service, source lag, SoC and two-sided DC-energy boundary.

sources.title: Configuration-Constrained Tube MPC for Periodic Operation
sources.inspection: Fresh primary author full HTML and abstract version metadata.
sources.defined_boundary: Robust forward-invariant periodic tubes for uncertain LDIs; state containment and a terminal recovery connection preserve feasibility. A fixed economic criterion gives convergence to an optimal periodic tube.
sources.scope_limit: General LDI framework with an optimizable artificial periodic target. It is a preprint, not direct evidence for a fixed externally imposed converter service contract.

sources.title: Consideration of Control-Loop Interaction in Transient Stability of Grid-Following Inverters using Bandwidth Separation Method
sources.defined_boundary: ROA in DVC current/squared-DC-voltage and PLL coordinates; initial and clearing states, bandwidth separation and restart energy determine recovery. The DVC-PLL interaction can destroy stability despite synchronization.
sources.scope_limit: Reduced analysis idealizes inner current tracking, with constant or step input power. Hardware-in-loop evidence includes a rectangular current limiter and chopper. No signed slow-service phase/SoC certificate is supplied.

sources.title: The Impact of Different Current Limiting Strategies on the Dynamic Behavior of Terminal Voltage in Grid-Following Converter After Faults
sources.defined_boundary: A post-fault feedback mechanism under d-axis priority links lower terminal voltage, lost active transfer, rising DC voltage and current saturation, preventing voltage recovery.
sources.scope_limit: No quantitative state/phase feasibility region; authors explicitly leave LVRT-control interaction and quantitative recovery/stability-region analysis for future work.

null_model.status: Elementary derivation authored in this audit; not a simulation or claim about the locked GFL controller.
assumptions: No losses, source clipping/ramp saturation, DC feedback or converter-current dynamics.
null_model.meaning: Off-peak energy extrema are a standard lag/integration consequence. Two-sided energy headroom is elementary. For phase-independent piecewise-linear fault dynamics the phase dependence remains c(t)+a(t)sin(phi)+b(t)cos(phi). This is a null hypothesis to rule out before claiming a new physical mechanism.
null_model.limits: The full converter fault maximizer need not occur at these energy extrema. No generic direction or size of its phase shift is asserted.

falsification_conditions: The claimed phase shift and admissible sectors reduce to this LTI/trigonometric null and standard periodic predecessor sets.
A claimed impossibility rests only on failure of one fixed controller rather than a control-independent necessary bound.
Improvement vanishes when the dynamic P/Q allocator and periodic MPC receive identical measurements, preview, actuator limits, service-error bounds and recovery definitions.
Claimed full recovery resets hidden state, ignores battery inventory or changes the forcing clock/phase.
A theorem without a controlled approximation error fails to transfer to the frozen averaged model.
interpretation_of_mpc_collision: Matching an ordinary periodic-MPC frontier defeats a new-controller-superiority claim but does not by itself refute an independently new, tight analytic resource theorem. The latter must contribute beyond elementary energy integration or naming a standard viability set.
